one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-03 to 2026-11-01. AAOI's own Q3 2026 report is most likely just outside it: the last two Q3 reports came in the first week of November and Q2 2026 came 2026-08-06, and no Q3 date had been filed or released as of 2026-10-03 (EDGAR index), so I put roughly 15-20% on results or a pre-announcement landing inside the window. What does fall inside: (1) hyperscaler Q3 calls in late October (capex guidance drives the whole AI-optics group, and AAOI moved +/-10% on Corning and peer news in September); (2) peer prints in late October (Celestica, Corning, possibly Lumentum/Coherent/Fabrinet near the end of the window); (3) steady supply from the $600M ATM filed 2026-08-21 (about 5M shares at today's price, around 6% of float), a mild headwind; (4) possible 1.6T qualification or shipment news, since management said late-Q3 deliveries would follow qualification. No clear direction: short-term momentum is negative (-46% over 3 months, ATM overhang) but short interest is high at 14.5% of shares. So I centre a lognormal slightly below spot (median about $114) with a monthly sigma of about 0.36, a little below 139%/3.5=0.40 because the window probably has no earnings print. P(>= spot) is 0.48.

fair_value.method: Blend of a forward P/E on my estimate of next-twelve-month EPS as of Oct 2027 ($5.00 x 22x = $110, weight 0.65) and a 5-year DCF (WACC 12.5%, terminal growth 4%, terminal FCF margin 13%, about 100M diluted shares = $64, weight 0.35). Blended fair value is about $94.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) non-GAAP EPS $5.00 x 22x forward P/E (peer median 32.9x, range 15.8-49.9x)

inputs_detail.value: ~$1.1B; capacity-constrained, demand > capacity through mid-2027; $200M 1.6T order in hand

inputs_detail.derivation: 800G/1.6T capacity >930k units/month by YE2026 (call). At roughly 50% effective output (DSP/TIA component limits cited on the call) and a blended ASP near $550, datacenter revenue is about $250M/month (~$3B/yr) at full ramp. Adding CATV at ~$325M/yr and assuming the ramp is reached through 2027 gives $3.0B for Q4'27-Q3'28, a little above FY2027 consensus of $2.8B.
Q2 2026 29.8%, Q3 guide 29-30.5%, CEO said Q4 'maybe 32, 33%', long-term target ~40%. I use 33% because 1.6T ramp costs and the history of under-delivering argue against assuming the 40% target.
Q2 2026 non-GAAP gross profit ~$57M less non-GAAP net income $5.5M implies ~$52M/quarter of opex+interest+tax. I scale it to ~$80M/quarter for the larger Texas/Ningbo footprint (8-Ks) and higher R&D.

84.9M outstanding 2026-08-20 (424B5), plus ~5M from the $600M ATM at ~$115, plus 2.9M from converting $124.9M of notes at $43.31, plus ~1.3M vested Amazon warrants (strike $23.70), plus 1.7M RSU/PSU = ~95M. I add ~5M for further raises, since H1 capex+prepayments were $625M against -$74M operating cash flow.

$3.0B x 33% = $990M gross profit, less $320M opex = $670M operating income; 15% tax gives ~$570M, or $5.70/share on 100M shares. I haircut 12% for execution risk (AAOI's history of slips, top-3 customers = 93% of revenue) to get $5.00, close to the low-to-middle of the FY2027 consensus range.

12-peer median forward P/E is 32.9x (range 15.8-49.9x). The direct transceiver comparables, Innolight 15.8x and Eoptolink 18.7x, have higher margins, and contract-manufacturing peers FN and CLS trade at about 25x. AAOI has lower gross margin (~30% vs 35-40%+), top-10 customers at 99% of revenue, negative FCF and repeated dilution, so I put it below the median, between the Chinese transceiver makers and FN/CLS. I see no structural advantage that would justify a premium, apart from US manufacturing for tariff/China-ban-sensitive buyers, which is real but unproven in pricing.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue 2027-2031 $2.4B/$3.3B/$4.0B/$4.4B/$4.6B; FCF margin -5%/8%/11%/13%/13%; WACC 12.5%; terminal growth 4%; net cash ~$200M; ~100M shares; valued at Oct 2027

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 is set below the $2.8B consensus to reflect ramp risk, then growth slows to mid-single digits by 2031 as the 800G/1.6T cycle matures; CATV ~$325M/yr per management.

H1 2026 operating cash flow was -$73.8M and capex plus prepayments were $625M. Management said H2 capex intensity will be higher than H1, so 2027 stays negative. Mature FCF margin = ~33-35% GM less ~10% opex less tax less maintenance capex of ~6-7% of sales.
High-beta small/mid cap with 139% realized vol, 14.5% short interest and customer concentration; equity cost about 12-13% with negligible debt weight.
$508.8M cash and $186.4M debt at 2026-06-30, plus up to $600M ATM, less heavy H2 capex and prepayments.

bear.story: 1.6T ramp slips or share is lost to Innolight/Eoptolink/Coherent; a hyperscaler concentrated at 24-26% of revenue cuts orders, or AI capex digests in 2027; GM stays near 28-30%; the ATM and new raises keep diluting. NTM EPS ~$2.50 x 18x = $45. AAOI fell ~90% from its 2017 peak when its main datacenter customer shifted, which is the precedent.

base.story: Capacity ramps with slips; 2027 revenue ~$2.4-2.8B, GM 32-34%, non-GAAP EPS reaches ~$5 NTM by late 2027; multiple compresses to 22x as growth slows and peers de-rate; dilution to ~100M shares.

bull.story: 930k+ units/month sold out through 2027, 1.6T and CPO lasers add share at a second hyperscaler, GM moves toward 35-40%, US-made supply wins share as China optics face restrictions; NTM EPS ~$7.50 x 28-30x.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 22x NTM P/E, about 33% below the 32.9x peer median and inside the range: above the two direct Chinese transceiver comparables (15.8x/18.7x) and slightly below FN/CLS (~25x). AAOI itself trades at 50x forward on StockAnalysis's NTM basis.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount should last through the horizon for structural reasons: (1) non-GAAP gross margin ~30% vs 35-40%+ at Coherent/Innolight, with management's own 40% target framed as long-term; (2) extreme concentration: top 10 customers 99% and top 3 at 42/26/24% of Q2 revenue, with Digicomm alone $211M of $314M receivables (10-Q); (3) negative FCF (-$900M TTM) funded by three equity raises in 2026, so per-share value keeps leaking; (4) history of cyclical collapse on customer loss. The partial offset is US/Texas manufacturing capacity, which is valuable if China-made transceivers are restricted. That is why I sit above the Chinese peers and do not use their multiple.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$55 (about 1-in-5 odds on my ladder) the market cap would be ~$5B on a business guiding to $1.1B of 2026 revenue and capacity for several billion. For the stock to get there, the 800G/1.6T ramp would almost certainly have failed: lost qualification or share at the key hyperscaler, a large order cut, or margins stuck below 28% so the capex cannot earn a return. Ordinary volatility at 139% realized vol explains $70-80 more easily, which is why the break level sits lower.

reasoning: Primary documents show a company scaling fast but burning cash. Q2 2026 revenue was $191.9M (+86% y/y), datacenter $107.7M and CATV $80.6M, with the first non-GAAP profit of $0.06. Q3 guidance is $255-290M, management talks of ~$1.1B for 2026, a $200M 1.6T order in hand, and 800G/1.6T capacity rising from ~200k to >930k units/month by year-end. Against that, H1 capex plus equipment prepayments were $625M against -$74M operating cash flow. A $600M ATM came on 2026-08-21, the third raise of 2026 after the public offering of 7.8M shares (net $1.03B in H1). The 8-Ks show the build-out (FAB4 cleanroom $94M, Houston building bought for $26.8M, Hightower Buildings 4/5, a new 38k sqm Ningbo plant, RMB 500M credit line), so more capital calls are likely. Customer concentration is extreme (99% top-10). Insider activity is limited to officer sales of vested RSU/PSU (Form 144s). The stock is $115.59, down ~50% from the June high of $233.67. I value it at ~$94: 22x my NTM EPS of $5.00 as of Oct 2027 (P/E, 65%), cross-checked by a DCF at $64 (35%). The multiple is below the 12-peer median of 32.9x because of lower margins, concentration and dilution. Scenarios: bear $45 (30%), base $110 (45%), bull $215 (25%), probability-weighted mean ~$116 and median ~$105. I built the ladder from a mixture of three lognormals (sigma 0.50/0.32/0.35), which gives a wide distribution in line with 139% realized vol but not as wide as a pure 139%-vol lognormal, because fundamentals bound the bear case near tangible book of ~$26/share after the raises. P(>= spot $116) is about 0.43, slightly below 50%: my fair value is below spot and dilution is ongoing, offset by a fat right tail if the 1.6T ramp works. Research limits: Alpha Vantage and Twelve Data fundamentals were unavailable (rate limit/plan), so consensus comes from StockAnalysis and a Tickflow search snippet. Peer EV/EBITDA is trailing, not forward.
